title: Aster Bikes Mobile Repair Full Case
description: One original synthetic five-stage consulting case with a deterministic questioning rubric.

fullCases.title: Mobile repair van rollout
fullCases.situation: Aster Bikes, a fictional regional bicycle retailer, piloted mobile repair vans in three districts. Management must decide where and how to expand the service next quarter without weakening contribution or service quality.

questioning.title: Aster Bikes mobile repair rollout
questioning.situation: Aster Bikes completed a three-district mobile repair pilot and must choose its next-quarter rollout plan.
questioning.objective: Ask the questions needed to clarify the decision and diagnose the strongest expansion district.

intents.label: Success definition
intents.feedback: Clarify the decision criteria and the time horizon for results.
referenceQuestions: What defines a successful rollout, and over what time horizon?

intents.label: Decision scope
intents.feedback: Define which districts or neighborhoods are eligible for expansion.
referenceQuestions: Which districts or neighborhoods are in scope for expansion?

intents.label: Demand quality
intents.feedback: Compare booking volume and repeat demand by district.
referenceQuestions: How do booking volume and repeat use differ across districts?

intents.label: Unit economics
intents.feedback: Compare contribution and costs by district.
referenceQuestions: What contribution and costs does each district generate?

intents.label: Operating feasibility
intents.feedback: Test mechanic capacity and the constraints on a next-quarter rollout.
referenceQuestions: Can mechanic capacity meet service targets within the fleet and next-quarter constraints?

structure.title: Structure the mobile repair decision
structure.situation: The three pilot districts produced different demand, economics, and service performance.
structure.objective: Determine whether and where Aster Bikes should expand mobile repair next quarter.

hypotheses.label: Expand first in districts where repeat demand and reliable operations sustain attractive contribution.
hypotheses.rationale: This hypothesis is market-specific and links the decision to demand, economics, and execution.

hypotheses.label: Expand every district because all three pilots completed some repairs.
hypotheses.rationale: Completing some repairs does not establish sufficient demand, economics, or operating reliability.

branchOptions.label: Customer demand
branchOptions.description: Bookings, repeat use, customer segments, and addressable demand.

branchOptions.label: Unit economics
branchOptions.description: Contribution per job, route costs, and break-even volume.

branchOptions.label: Operational feasibility
branchOptions.description: Mechanic capacity, completion rates, travel time, and service quality.

branchOptions.label: Rollout and risk
branchOptions.description: District sequencing, pilot gates, capital needs, and downside controls.

branchOptions.label: Corporate brand campaign
branchOptions.description: A retailer-wide advertising refresh independent of repair-pilot performance.

modelStructure.title: Customer demand
questions: Does demand repeat after the initial trial?

modelStructure.title: Unit economics
questions: What contribution does each completed job generate?
Which districts cover van and mechanic costs?

modelStructure.title: Operational feasibility
questions: Can completion rates remain high at greater volume?
Where are the mechanic or routing constraints?

modelStructure.title: Rollout and risk
questions: What evidence should trigger the next expansion?

exhibit.title: Mobile repair pilot performance
exhibit.description: Average weekly results during the final month of the pilot.

visualization.title: Aster Bikes pilot performance by district

questions.prompt: Using the River row, what weekly contribution does the mobile repair pilot generate?

explanation.short: Multiply weekly bookings by the completion rate and contribution per completed job.

brainstorming.title: Improve mobile repair performance
brainstorming.context: Aster Bikes can test three actions during the next eight weeks before committing to more vans.
brainstorming.question: Which actions should Aster Bikes prioritize to improve demand, economics, and service reliability?

ideas.label: Offer recurring maintenance slots to high-frequency riders.
Discount every repair indefinitely without measuring repeat use.
Cluster appointments geographically before assigning each van.
Let each van cross the entire region for every individual booking.
Test a minimum service fee for distant appointments.
Buy a full regional fleet before testing another district.

synthesis.title: Recommend the mobile repair rollout
synthesis.situation: The pilot shows meaningful differences in contribution, repeat demand, and completion rates by district.
synthesis.decision: Recommend the next-quarter mobile repair rollout.
facts: River generates $11,900 of weekly contribution with an 85% completion rate and 42% repeat rate.
Hill generates $8,640 of weekly contribution with a 75% completion rate and 34% repeat rate.
South generates $5,040 of weekly contribution with a 60% completion rate and 20% repeat rate.

recommendation.label: Expand River first, improve Hill, and pause South.

evidence.label: River has the strongest weekly contribution, completion rate, and repeat rate.
All vans display the same Aster Bikes brand.

risk.label: River's completion rate may fall as appointment volume grows.
The accounting office may move next year.

nextStep.label: Run an eight-week River capacity and repeat-demand test with explicit gates.
Purchase a regional van fleet before another test.

synthesis.modelClose: Aster Bikes should expand mobile repair in River first because it leads the pilot on weekly contribution, completion, and repeat use. The main risk is that service quality falls at higher volume, so the next step is an eight-week River capacity and repeat-demand test with explicit performance gates.
